1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bg5 Be7 5.e3 h6 6.Bh4 O-O 7.Bd3 {7.Nf3 is more
usual} 7...b6 8.cxd5 Nxd5 9.Bxe7 Qxe7 10.Nxd5 exd5 11.Nf3 c5 12.O-O c4 {
Trying to unbalance the position, where the strongest player has more 
oportunities to win.} 13.Bb1 Nd7 14.Qc2 Nf6 15.Ne5 {The plan for Black is 
clear, to advance the Queenside pawns and try to open lines in this flank 
but what is the plan for White for attack on the Kingside?} 15...g6 {
Trying to exchange bishops after Bf5 but at the same time weakening his 
Kingside} 16.Qe2 Bb7 17.f4 {The white rook is going to attack from f3 
after the advance of the White Kingside pawns. Now there are several 
breaks in the 5th line. To remove the White Knight from his stronghold in 
e5 black has to play f6 - weakening more his Kingside - or Nd7 and Nxe5 
giving a strong square in f6 for a Rook and the doubling or tripling the 
heavy pieces on the "f" column, from here there is always the posibility 
of a sacrifice on g6} 17...Kg7 18.Rf3 Rac8 19.g4 c3 20.bxc3 Rxc3 21.Bd3 {
To give way to the QR and avoid the check on c1} 21...Qa3 {Black is 
increasing the pressure on the Queenside but White will break in the 
Kingside. The balance is unclear.} 22.g5 hxg5 23.fxg5 Ne4 24.Raf1 Nxg5 {
Something must be done against the threat Rxf7} 25.Rg3 Rxd3 {If White 
accepts the offered exchange than Black's position will be satisfactory.} 
26.Rxg5 Rxe3 27.Qf2 {White is penetrating trough f6 and also the sacrifice
in g6 is pending.} 27...Rxe5 {As the Black Queen cannot retreat because 
the rook will be undefended, Black sacrifices the exchange to get rid of 
one of the attackers.} 28.Qf6+ Kh6 29.Rxe5 Ba6 30.Qf4+ Kg7 31.Re3 Qb4 32.
Qf6+ 1-0
